about: Minimized regression vectors of the issue #196 differential fuzz: each divergence the campaigns found, minimized, and agreement vectors at boundaries the generated corpus does not cross (`agrees`: why both sides answer alike). `origin` says where a vector came from: the campaign case it was minimized from, or that it was written by hand (after a run-3 case of the first campaign, generator e62f427, whose inputs no commit on this branch regenerates). Each runs in its own environment (its `did`); the Rust driver records the reference verdict into tests/goldens/differential/corpus.jsonl, and the TypeScript replay holds each either to agreement (`agrees`) or to the exact symptom listed for its case id, with its issue, in tests/goldens/differential/divergences.json. A vector stays for good (#62): when its divergence is fixed, it becomes an agreement vector.

vectors.name: reference_refuses_identical_func
vectors.note: A func reference written and read at the same type func (L) -> () with L = record { a : L }. The candid crate rewrites the uninhabited record L in the wire table to empty (TypeEnv::replace_empty) but not in the expected type, so its subtype check becomes L <: empty and fails: it refuses identical types. The runtime accepts. Reference bug.
vectors.did:
type L = record { a : L };
type F = func (L) -> ();

vectors.name: reference_absorbs_identical_func_in_opt
vectors.note: The same func reference under opt, read at its own type: the reference's failed subtype check is absorbed by the opt, so it decodes null; the runtime decodes the reference. Reference bug (same cause).

vectors.name: reference_accepts_non_subtype_func
vectors.note: A func () -> (W) read at func () -> (E) with W = record { x : W } and E = record { y : E }: W lacks E's required field y, so the wire type is not a subtype. The reference rewrites W to empty and accepts (empty <: E); the runtime refuses type_mismatch. Reference bug (same cause, the other direction).

vectors.name: reference_skips_invalid_utf8_method
vectors.note: An extra func argument whose method name is the single byte ff (not UTF-8), skipped because no argument is expected. The reference skips it without checking (it does check a skipped text, and refuses this name when it decodes the func); the runtime refuses invalid_utf8. Reference bug.

vectors.name: future_type_reference_count

vectors.name: reference_quota_skipped_vec

vectors.agrees: Both accept: the reference's quota is sized from the message, so it judges it.

vectors.name: contract_declarations_absent

vectors.name: reference_reads_func_from_empty_wire
vectors.note: One argument whose wire type is empty, followed by the bytes of a func reference, read at a func type. No value has type empty, yet the reference decodes aaaaa-aa.f: it reads a reference value through its subtype relation alone, where empty <: t holds. The runtime refuses type_mismatch. Reference bug (#227, item 2).
vectors.origin: written by hand after run-3 case d/1012392/198

vectors.name: reference_unsound_subtype_memo
vectors.note: func () -> (W3) read at func () -> (E3). W7 <: E7 is false (W5 has an arm x that V lacks), and the reference refuses W7 at E7 on its own; but checking W3 <: E3 visits c : opt W5 first, assumes (W5, V), proves (W7, E7) under that assumption, retracts (W5, V) when x fails (the opt rule then accepts c), and keeps (W7, E7) in its memo, so v : W7 <: E7 is answered true. The runtime refuses type_mismatch. Reference bug (unsound coinductive memo).

vectors.name: label_collision_numbered_field
vectors.note: record { x : record { 100 : text } } where another declaration writes the same canonical record as record { d : text } (the label hash of d is 100). The field-name table attaches names to canonical nodes, so the runtime keys B's field as d; the reference (and the source) say 100. Same bytes, same id, different domain key.
vectors.did:
type A = record { c : record { d : text } };
type B = record { x : record { 100 : text } };

vectors.name: depth_opt_128_levels
vectors.note: opt T0 nested 128 levels. The runtime charges its deepest node 255 depth steps (measured), the most a decoded opt node of a Contract-loaded schema can be charged within maxDepth 256: every edge there is a rec thunk, so a decoded node at level L and the rec hop reaching it are both charged 2L + 1. Even charges come from a blob's bytes (one step below the blob) and from skipped or absorbed wire values (one step per wire level); the vectors charged exactly 256 are depth_variant_blob_126_arms, chain_opt_blob_127_levels, chain_record_blob_127_levels, skip_field_vec_255_levels and absorbed_vec_255_levels.
vectors.agrees: Both accept: the deepest opt node within the runtime's maxDepth (255 steps).
